texts.preamble: Santosh Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 March, 2020 Author: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that on 26.05.2007, Food Inspector-Arvind Kumar has made an inspection in the shop of petitioner namely Milen Sweets. After giving his introduction, the Food Inspector asked him for food license. After inspection, the Food Inspector has purchased 6 packets of "Mirch Sev" and after following the rules prescribed in this regard, he sent the sample for examination. The samples were found mis-branded, thus, he launched the prosecution against the petitioner and his father who died during trial.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the learned Courts 2 CRR-1096-2020 below erred in convicting the applicant. The Court has only examined the Food Inspector as prosecution witnesses Santosh Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161557607/ 1 whereas one Suresh Gupta who is said to be the witness, has not been examined by the prosecution, however, he has been examined as defence witness. He further submits that and there is no independent witnesses in this case who supported to the prosecution story. The learned Court below has also committed the legal error in understanding the deference between the ward 'packed' and 'pre-packed' which denotes the system of packing. The Court considered the samples as pack nature in some of the paras of judgment but at conclusion, the Court has considered the samples as pre packed, which shows contradictory approach of the trial Court. The public analyst has also not not examined by the prosecution and an application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. for the same purpose has been rejected by the trial Court. The seized product has not been produced before the trial Court, moreover, the Food Inspector has not mentioned the contents which are written in on the alleged level. The Food Inspector has also refused that the 'Sev' was in packed condition. The prosecution has also not complied with the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act for issuance of notice. He further submits that the entire prosecution framed against the applicant is an excessive jurisdiction of the State. The prosecution also suffers from non-joinder of necessary party as the Om Industries are the original manufacture of 'sev' and involved in the packaging of the same. The applicant only bought the same from Om Industries and sell it accordingly. The case of prosecution does not found under the definition of mis-branded. He also argued that under section 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the maximum penalty for sub-standard food or branding is only fine. It is also submitted that the provisions of the said Act being beneficial to the accused persons can be applied with respect to earlier cases as well, which are pending in the Court. He has also produced the copy of order passed by co-ordinate bench of this Court in the case of Pawan Kumar Goswami Vs. State of M.P. passed in 3 CRR-1096-2020 Cr.R 5136/2019 , dated 13/11/2019. Apart from that the applicant is suffering from cardiac disease and if he does not release on bail, he would suffer adversely. With the aforesaid he prays for allowing this application. On the other hand learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the submissions.
